label: D2 after a rare transition a2 -> S1
explanation: Fires only at the DELAY_2 step, and only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1 (the rare transition for a2). It is a conjunction of the observed state and last-action inputs at that step. Dev split: precision 1.0, recall 0.995, mass recall 0.9998. It never fires at D1 or GO, on common transitions (a2->S2, a1->S1), or on the other rare transition (a1->S2). The misses are tiny activations (<0.12 of max) at a1->S1c D2 steps, mostly right after an earlier a2->S1 rare event. Activation is near-saturated (median 3.7, max 4.6). From the example quartiles, the lowest activations show up after long runs of common trials and the highest when there was an earlier a2->S1 rare event in the window, but I only checked this informally. The obvious alternative (action==2 & common==0) is identical and observable at D2, so no future variable is needed.

issues: Minor inaccuracy in the miss description: the test misses (340 steps, 0.0% of activation mass, all at most about 0.02 of max) happen at both a1->S1 and a2->S2 common D2 steps, not only a1->S1. Test scores: a2 common D2 gave precision 0.0007 (about 118 steps), a1 common D2 gave 0.0017 (about 222 steps). This is negligible residual noise, often seen when an earlier a2->S1 rare event is in the window.

All factual claims check out on the test split. phase != D2: precision 0, mass recall 0. a1->S2 rare D2: precision 0, mass recall 0. The predicate has 0 false positives. The action==2 & common==0 form gives identical scores.
The magnitude claim (strongest after an earlier a2->S1 rare event) was not scored and is still only an eye-check. It does not affect the label.
